headlines: Black Friday half session, US stocks close 1pm ET (18:00Z)
SPY 726.28 +1.34% at 17:00Z, then a ~$1 drop candle to 725.85 at 17:06Z; QQQ +1.88%, IWM +1.58%, GLD +1.58%, TLT -1.20% (Stocklake)
VIX 26.86 and Fear&Greed 24.5 (extreme fear) from 16:09Z snapshot, VIX up from 25.21 in the prior snapshot despite the rally; SPY RSI 42.8; breadth 4.4% oversold vs 3.3% overbought
Stocktwits trending: TSLA +4.9%, VRTX -5.5% (rebounding off 503 low), KSS +3.1%, EWZ +10.1%, NTSK +7.2%, KWEB +4.7%, RBLX +4.9%, GOOGL flat after fading from 281; causes not found
Stocktwits SPY message volume HIGH (55); sentiment split 50.5 bull / 49.5 bear
Web search found no same-day market coverage

rumors.text: Packed malls, shoppers spending big on Black Friday
rumors.why: Anecdotal; strong holiday spending would support retail names and consumer confidence

rumors.text: China state support driving the global bounce (KWEB +4.7%, EWZ +10%); carried over, still unconfirmed
rumors.why: Would support risk appetite; stale story, price action consistent but cause unverified

rumors.text: Media is targeting NVIDIA to shake holders out; NVDA ~148.9, down ~12% from Nov 23 high after a 125-175 swing
rumors.why: Opinion; if NVDA weakness is only noise it would remove a drag on QQQ/SPY

rumors.text: SPY will squeeze through the top then reverse; calls for a 716 close
rumors.why: Opinion only; would mean the holiday rally fades into the close

plays.reason: SPY still holding most of the reversal (+1.3%) with QQQ/IWM leading; half-days tend to drift with the session trend, but a fresh $1 drop candle, rising VIX and split crowd make this near a coin flip
plays.catalyst: Thin-volume drift into the 1pm ET half-day close

readings.whats_new: SPY edged up from 725.38 to a 726.28 high near 17:00Z, then dropped about $1 in one candle to 725.85, so last hour's up-into-close play is only marginally ahead. VIX snapshot rose to 26.86 (from 25.21) and Fear&Greed to 24.5 even as stocks rallied, a fear-vs-price divergence. New trending names: KSS, NTSK, KWEB, RBLX; cup-and-handle chatter replaced by squeeze-then-fade and packed-malls posts.
